title: Before creation
hookLine: when no form was seen, no sin or virtue, no sun or moon, He alone was (Sukhmani 21)

lines: WHERE WAS I BEFORE I WAS BORN?
BEFORE THE TOWN? BEFORE THE WORLD?
cards: Children are very good at one kind of question. Where was I before I was born? What was there before the house?
Before the town? Before the world? Each answer moves the question back a step, until a parent says, gently, that's enough for tonight.
The first stanza of Sukhmani's twenty-first ashtpadi asks those child's questions on purpose, one after another, and sends no one to bed. It walks them all the way back, to before creation.

teach.h: JAB: A STRING OF WHEN QUESTIONS.
teach.b: The stanza is built from questions, each beginning jab, when.

teach.h: NO FORM, NO GRUDGE, NO SORROW.
teach.b: In paraphrase: when there was no form to be seen, where would sin or virtue have come from? When He was absorbed in the stillness, against whom could anyone hold a grudge?
When there was no color or mark, who could feel joy or sorrow? When there was only the Supreme, by Himself, who could be caught in attachment or doubt?
Then the closing line: He set His own play in motion, and Nanak says, there is no other maker. Look at what the questions do.
They take what fills an ordinary day, right and wrong, grudges, happiness, grief, worry, and quietly show that, in this picture, none of it is the floor. Before it, under it, there was the One.
Yesterday's hymn in raag Maru fills in the sky for the same scene: no day or night, no moon or sun, only the One, in stillness.
The word for form here is akaar: shape, outline, something you can see.
Before creation there was no akaar at all. And notice what the stanza doesn't say. It doesn't call joys and sorrows fake.
In its picture they belong to the play; they just aren't the deepest thing. There's a strange comfort in that.
Whatever you're carrying this week, the grudge or the worry, there was a time before it, and Sukhmani says the One who was there then is here now.

how: Sikhs reciting Sukhmani Sahib's twenty-first ashtpadi hear a series of when-questions about the time before creation, each answered by the One alone.

o: the first day, when the sun and moon were made
an empty nothing, with nothing and no one in it
the stillness when only the One was, before any form

s: the stanza says our joys and sorrows are fake
they're real and belong to the play; they're just not the deepest thing.
the stanza is built from a string of questions
each begins jab, when, and walks back to before creation.
the stanza names a helper who made the world with God
its closing line says there is no other maker.

games.q: the stanza asks: before any form, when there was only the One, who could hold a grudge? what's the answer it points to?
o: no one: there was only the One.
games.why: no one. with no form and no other, there was nothing to quarrel with. the One alone was, and set the play in motion.

practice: Close your eyes and let the room fade, the furniture, then the walls, the street, the city, the earth, the sun, like lights going out one at a time, and rest in the dark and the quiet before anything.
Then slowly let things return, and notice what's still here. If you pray, rest in Waheguru in the stillness.

wordCard.voice: Before creation. Sukhmani asks: with no form yet, no grudge or sorrow, what was there? Its answer: the One alone, setting the play in motion.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: akaar, form or shape; before creation, no akaar could be seen.

carryVoice: Your line: he alone was. Before every worry, and under it, the One. See you tomorrow.
